issues.title: Missing .inc file nodes causing dropped import edges
issues.description: Five import edges were dropped because target .inc file nodes do not exist in the graph. The .inc files exist on disk but were never extracted as nodes.
issues.recommendation: Ensure .inc files are processed by the extractor. Add *.inc to the file patterns for extraction or create nodes for generated/include files that are imported by source files.

issues.title: Most .c files have no extracted functions
issues.description: Only 47 out of 117 .c files (40%) have functions extracted. Core runtime files like jl_uv.c, array.c, builtins.c, init.c, interpreter.c, jltypes.c, method.c, module.c have zero functions in the graph despite containing many function definitions.
issues.recommendation: Investigate extractor configuration. Likely causes: (1) static functions are skipped, (2) functions with JL_DLLEXPORT/JL_CANSAFEPOINT macros not recognized, (3) C parser not handling Julia's code style. Review extractor patterns for C function detection.

issues.title: 191 .ua/.trash config files pollute graph
issues.description: 191 config nodes from .ua/.trash directory (previous run artifacts) are included in the graph as orphan nodes with no edges. These are not part of the Julia codebase.
issues.recommendation: Exclude .ua/.trash and .ua/intermediate directories from extraction. Add ignore patterns to the extraction configuration.

issues.title: 598 orphan nodes with no edges
issues.description: 598 nodes have no incoming or outgoing edges. Includes 191 .ua/.trash config files, 174 document nodes, and many config files that are not connected to the code graph.
issues.recommendation: Filter out nodes with no edges during assembly, or ensure extraction creates proper relationships for all node types.

issues.title: Header files lack function declarations
issues.description: 80 out of 89 .h files have no contained functions. While headers typically contain declarations not definitions, the graph could benefit from tracking declarations for cross-reference analysis.
issues.recommendation: Consider extracting function declarations from headers as separate nodes (type: 'declaration') to enable header-to-implementation tracing.

issues.title: 15 empty batch files
issues.description: 15 batch files contributed zero nodes and edges. These represent wasted extraction effort.
issues.recommendation: Investigate why these batches are empty. May indicate files that couldn't be parsed or empty directories.

issues.title: 99 duplicate node IDs removed during assembly
issues.description: 99 duplicate node IDs were found across batches (kept last). This indicates overlapping batch boundaries or re-processing of same files.
issues.recommendation: Review batch partitioning strategy to minimize overlap. Ensure each file is assigned to exactly one batch.

recommendations: Priority 1: Fix extractor to capture functions from all .c files (especially core runtime)
Priority 2: Add .inc file extraction to resolve 5 missing import edges
Priority 3: Exclude .ua/.trash and intermediate directories from extraction
Priority 4: Filter orphan nodes or ensure all extracted nodes have relationships
Priority 5: Investigate and fix empty batch files
Priority 6: Review batch partitioning to eliminate duplicate node IDs
